iterations.theme: Priprema pashalne večere i navještaj izdaje u Markovu evanđelju (Mk 14): Isusovo proročko znanje, Judina izdaja i poziv na osobno ispitivanje savjesti

sections.subtitle: Prvi dan beskvasnih kruhova: zašto je Marku važno da je četvrtak
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković objašnjava vremenski okvir prvog dana beskvasnih kruhova i židovsko računanje dana
sections.content:
Nova epizoda serijala posvećenog Markovu evanđelju počinje pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija“ koji voditelj **Stanko Stojić** upućuje gledateljima, slušateljima i, kako ih sam naziva, „štiocima Markova evanđelja“. Uz gosta, **fra Antu Vučkovića**, stigao je do sredine 14. poglavlja i teme koja otvara završni čin evanđeoske drame: pripreme za pashalnu večeru. Isus šalje učenike, a Stojić predlaže da se tekst rastumači od samog početka, od izraza „prvog dana beskvasnih kruhova“.

Fra Ante Vučković najprije upozorava na precizno vođenje vremena kod Marka. Četrnaesto poglavlje počelo je napomenom da su „za dva dana“ Pasha i beskvasni kruhovi, što pada u srijedu. Sada se radnja pomaknula za jedan dan, na **četvrtak**. Četvrtak je bio dan priprave, a sama Pasha blagovala se, prema židovskom računanju, u petak.

Tu nastaje očita nepodudarnost s današnjim kalendarom, koju fra Ante objašnjava razlikom u računanju vremena. Po suvremenom shvaćanju riječ je o četvrtku navečer. **Židovi**, međutim, računaju da novi dan počinje sa zalaskom sunca, pa je ista večer za njih već bila petak. Bez obzira na sustav računanja, zaključuje gost, radnja se odvija u četvrtak, na dan kad počinje priprava za Pashu.
sections.subtitle_en: The First Day of Unleavened Bread: Why It Matters to Mark That It Is Thursday
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković explains the time frame of the first day of unleavened bread and the Jewish reckoning of days
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the series dedicated to the Gospel of Mark begins with the greeting "Praise be to Jesus and Mary" addressed by host **Stanko Stojić** to the viewers, listeners, and, as he himself calls them, "readers of the Gospel of Mark." Together with the guest, **fra Ante Vučković**, he has reached the middle of chapter 14 and the topic that opens the final act of the Gospel drama: preparation for the Passover meal. Jesus sends the disciples, and Stojić proposes that the text be interpreted from the very beginning, from the expression "on the first day of Unleavened Bread."

Fra Ante Vučković first draws attention to the precise keeping of time in Mark. The fourteenth chapter began with the note that "after two days" were the Passover and Unleavened Bread, which falls on Wednesday. Now the action has moved by one day, to **Thursday**. Thursday was the day of preparation, and the Passover itself was eaten, according to Jewish reckoning, on Friday.

Here an obvious discrepancy with today's calendar arises, which fra Ante explains by the difference in reckoning time. According to the modern understanding, it is Thursday evening. **The Jews**, however, reckon that a new day begins with sunset, so the same evening was already Friday for them. Regardless of the system of reckoning, the guest concludes, the action takes place on Thursday, on the day when the preparation for the Passover begins.

sections.subtitle: Što je značilo „pripraviti Pashu“: prostor, hrana i janje zaklano u Hramu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost nabraja što je sve bilo potrebno za pripremu pashalne večere
sections.content:
Fra Ante Vučković zatim objašnjava što je za jednog Židova u Isusovo vrijeme značila priprava Pashe. Nije to bila tek kuhinjska užurbanost, nego obvezan niz zadataka:

- osigurati **prostor** za blagovanje,
- spremiti **hranu**,
- dati obredno zaklati **janje** staro do godinu dana, i to u **Hramu**,
- sve dovršiti na vrijeme kako bi se Pasha mogla blagovati navečer.

Pasha se, naglašava gost, blagovala u noći i trebala je završiti oko dva sata ujutro, dakle iza ponoći. Takav je okvir, kako kaže, općenito vrijedio za sve Židove. Na tu se pozadinu nadovezuje konkretan evanđeoski prizor u kojem učenici pitaju Isusa: „Gdje hoćeš blagovati Pashu, da odemo i pripravimo?“
sections.subtitle_en: What It Meant to "Prepare the Passover": Space, Food, and a Lamb Slaughtered in the Temple
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest lists everything that was necessary for the preparation of the Passover meal
sections.content_en:
Fra Ante Vučković then explains what the preparation of the Passover meant for a Jew in Jesus' time. It was not merely kitchen haste, but an obligatory series of tasks:

- secure the **space** for dining,
- prepare the **food**,
- have ritually slaughtered a **lamb** up to one year old, and that in the **Temple**,
- finish everything on time so that the Passover could be eaten in the evening.

The Passover, the guest emphasizes, was eaten at night and was supposed to end around two o'clock in the morning, that is, after midnight. Such a framework, as he says, generally applied to all Jews. Concrete Gospel scene builds upon that background, in which the disciples ask Jesus: "Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?"

sections.subtitle: Upute koje odaju proročko znanje: Isus kao Učitelj
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković uspoređuje slanje učenika u grad sa slanjem po magarca prije ulaska u Jeruzalem
sections.content:
Odgovor koji Isus daje učenicima, prema fra Anti Vučkoviću, otkriva Njegovo **proročko znanje**. Gost podsjeća na sličan prizor obrađen ranije u serijalu, kada je Isus pred svečani ulazak u **Jeruzalem** poslao dvojicu učenika po magarca. Isto se znanje pokazuje i sada, ovaj put s još više pojedinosti. Isus šalje dvojicu učenika, za koje se ne zna tko su, u grad i govori im što će naći, na koga će naići i što trebaju reći. Najupečatljiviji je detalj čovjek koji nosi **krčag vode**, po kojem će ga prepoznati i kojega trebaju upitati za svratište.

Stanko Stojić dovršava misao gosta: radi se o svratištu u kojem će „Učitelj“ moći blagovati. Fra Ante se zadržava upravo na tom nazivu. Isusa ovdje Učiteljem nazivaju Njegovi učenici, a pri kraju evanđelja čitatelj već dobro zna kakav je bio odnos između njih i Njega.

„On je uistinu Učitelj“, ističe gost. Prema Markovu opisu, Isus je najviše vremena proveo poučavajući narod i svoje učenike. Nisu sve te pouke zapisane, nego je preneseno tek ponešto, u jezgrovitom obliku. Ipak, poučavanje je bilo glavnina Njegova javnog djelovanja.
sections.subtitle_en: Instructions That Reveal Prophetic Knowledge: Jesus as Teacher
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković compares sending the disciples into the city with sending for the donkey before the entrance into Jerusalem
sections.content_en:
The answer that Jesus gives to the disciples, according to fra Ante Vučković, reveals His **prophetic knowledge**. The guest recalls a similar scene discussed earlier in the series, when Jesus, before the solemn entry into **Jerusalem**, sent two disciples for a donkey. The same knowledge is shown now, this time with even more details. Jesus sends two disciples, whose identity is not known, into the city and tells them what they will find, whom they will encounter, and what they need to say. The most striking detail is a man carrying a **water jar**, by which they will recognize him and whom they are to ask for the guest room.

Stanko Stojić finishes the guest's thought: it is about a guest room in which the "Teacher" will be able to dine. Fra Ante dwells on precisely that title. Here, His disciples call Jesus Teacher, and near the end of the Gospel, the reader already knows well what the relationship between them and Him was like.

"He is truly the Teacher," the guest emphasizes. According to Mark's description, Jesus spent most of His time teaching the people and His disciples. Not all of those teachings were written down; rather, only some were conveyed, in a concise form. Nevertheless, teaching was the main part of His public ministry.

sections.subtitle: Dogovoreni znak ili svijest o vlastitoj sudbini?
sections.screenshot_description: Stanko Stojić pita je li čovjek s krčagom vode mogao biti unaprijed dogovoreni znak
sections.content:
Stojić iznosi tumačenje koje se ponekad čuje: možda je čovjek s krčagom bio **dogovoreni znak**, odnosno Isus se unaprijed dogovorio s nekim da će ondje nositi vodu. Fra Ante Vučković priznaje da bi tako nešto u današnjem svijetu bilo sasvim moguće i ne bi bilo sporno. Ovdje, međutim, nije riječ o dogovoru. Takvo bi „namještanje“, kaže, bilo potpuno neprimjereno svemu što se o Isusu dotad saznalo iz evanđelja.

Gost ističe da i sam taj detalj nije presudan. Čak i da se prihvati mogućnost dogovora, ostaje mnogo krupnija slika: **Isus zna što će se s Njim dogoditi**. Ono što čini, čini potpuno svjesno, jer se radi o utemeljiteljskom činu nečega što će trajati. To je način Njegove prisutnosti među vjernicima, prisutnost u **Euharistiji**.

Zato, prema fra Anti, nije bitno samo to što Isus predviđa čovjeka s krčagom, nego ulazak u znatno dublju priču. Sve što Ga čeka, četvrtak poslijepodne, petak, subota kao šabat u kojem se miruje i nedjelja uskrsnuća, Njemu je potpuno prisutno. On zna svoju sudbinu i svoj put, ali i ono što će se dogoditi s učenicima. U kratkim Markovim tekstovima Isus zna:

- tko Ga izdaje, zašto i na koji način,
- tko će Ga zatajiti, pa Petru precizno kaže što će se dogoditi,
- što će biti s Njim samim.

Učenicima je i ranije najavio da će Ga židovski i svećenički glavari uhvatiti, krivo optužiti, osuditi i sramotno pogubiti, ali da će treći dan uskrsnuti. Ta drama, koja stane u nekoliko riječi, prema gostu je drama odnosa Boga i čovjeka, Boga i Njegova izabranog naroda, i tiče se svih ljudi koji dolaze nakon toga.
sections.subtitle_en: An Arranged Sign or Awareness of One's Own Destiny?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Stanko Stojić asks whether the man with the water jar could have been a prearranged sign
sections.content_en:
Stojić presents an interpretation that is sometimes heard: perhaps the man with the jar was an **arranged sign**, that is, Jesus arranged in advance with someone that he would carry water there. Fra Ante Vučković admits that something like that in today's world would be entirely possible and would not be contentious. Here, however, it is not a matter of an arrangement. Such "rigging," he says, would be completely inappropriate to everything learned about Jesus from the Gospel up to that point.

The guest emphasizes that even that detail itself is not crucial. Even if one accepts the possibility of an arrangement, a much larger picture remains: **Jesus knows what will happen to Him**. What He does, He does completely consciously, because it is the foundational act of something that will endure. That is the manner of His presence among believers, presence in the **Eucharist**.

Therefore, according to fra Ante, it is not only important that Jesus foresees the man with the jar, but entering into a significantly deeper story. Everything that awaits Him—Thursday afternoon, Friday, Saturday as the Sabbath in which one rests, and the Sunday of the resurrection—is completely present to Him. He knows His destiny and His path, but also what will happen with the disciples. In Mark's short texts, Jesus knows:

- who is betraying Him, why, and in what manner,
- who will deny Him, so He tells Peter precisely what will happen,
- what will happen to Himself.

He had also announced to the disciples earlier that the Jewish leaders and chief priests would seize Him, falsely accuse Him, condemn Him, and shamefully execute Him, but that He would rise on the third day. That drama, which fits into a few words, according to the guest, is the drama of the relationship between God and man, God and His chosen people, and concerns all people who come after that.

sections.subtitle: Bez panike i bez emotivnih efekata: suverenost na putu prema križu
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković naglašava Isusovu suverenost i odsutnost emotivne dramatizacije
sections.content:
Fra Ante Vučković posebno ističe ton kojim Isus govori u tim trenucima. U tekstu nema emotivne drame. Isus ne stvara ozračje dramatičnosti kojim bi snažnim emocijama privukao učenike. Govori iz znanja koje posjeduje i iz **jasne suverenosti**: to je put kojim želi proći i koji prihvaća.

Stanko Stojić to sažima kolokvijalno: Isus „ne diže paniku“. Gost se slaže i zaključuje da je priprava za Pashu ujedno priprava za **Posljednju večeru** s učenicima. U njoj će se spojiti ono što Pasha znači Židovima, ono što je ta večer tada značila učenicima i ono što će kasnije značiti vjernicima. Taj spoj, kaže fra Ante, povezuje prošlost, sadašnjost i budućnost.
sections.subtitle_en: Without Panic and Without Emotional Effects: Sovereignty on the Way to the Cross
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković emphasizes Jesus' sovereignty and the absence of emotional dramatization
sections.content_en:
Fra Ante Vučković particularly emphasizes the tone with which Jesus speaks in those moments. There is no emotional drama in the text. Jesus does not create an atmosphere of dramatic tension with which to attract the disciples through strong emotions. He speaks from the knowledge He possesses and from **clear sovereignty**: that is the path He wishes to walk and which He accepts.

Stanko Stojić summarizes this colloquially: Jesus "does not cause panic." The guest agrees and concludes that the preparation for the Passover is at the same time the preparation for the **Last Supper** with the disciples. In it will merge what Passover means to the Jews, what that evening meant to the disciples then, and what it will later mean to believers. That union, fra Ante says, connects the past, the present, and the future.

sections.subtitle: „Doba vodenjaka“: kako new age čita Markov tekst
sections.screenshot_description: Stanko Stojić iznosi new age tumačenje čovjeka s krčagom kao astrološkog znaka vodenjaka
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim spominje ideju koju je vidio u jednom filmu, a koja se svojedobno često navodila. Neki pripadnici **new agea** čovjeka s krčagom vode tumače kao **vodenjaka**, odnosno astrološki znak. Prema tom čitanju Isus zaključuje kršćansko „doba ribe“ i najavljuje novo „doba vodenjaka“, poznatije kao „Age of Aquarius“, kako pjeva i istoimena pjesma.

Fra Ante Vučković takvo tumačenje odlučno odbacuje kao **nategnuto i proizvoljno**. U tekstu nema „apsolutno ničega“ osim simbolike koju netko tumači na svoj način. Simbolika ovdje znači samo jedno: to je čovjek kojega treba pitati za prostor. Izvlačiti iz toga da je Isus najavio doba vodenjaka nakon dvije tisuće godina doba ribe, kaže, posve je neutemeljeno. Ipak, priznaje da nekome tko nije ozbiljno prošao kroz Sveto pismo i pročita samo tu rečenicu takvo tumačenje može djelovati uvjerljivo.

Marko, ističe gost, ima sasvim drugi smjer i ne očekuje nikakvo buduće novo doba. **Novo doba dolazi s Kristom i Njegovim uskrsnućem**, a nakon toga slijedi ono što Isus najavljuje pri ustanovi Euharistije: da će piti novo vino u Kraljevstvu nebeskom. To je za Marka novo doba, a ne doba vodenjaka.
sections.subtitle_en: "The Age of Aquarius": How the New Age Reads Mark's Text
sections.screenshot_description_en: Stanko Stojić presents the New Age interpretation of the man with the water jar as the astrological sign of Aquarius
sections.content_en:
The host then mentions an idea he saw in a movie, which was frequently cited at one time. Some adherents of the **New Age** interpret the man with the water jar as **Aquarius**, that is, the astrological sign. According to that reading, Jesus concludes the Christian "age of Pisces" and announces a new "age of Aquarius," better known as the "Age of Aquarius," as sung in the song of the same name.

Fra Ante Vučković resolutely rejects such an interpretation as **far-fetched and arbitrary**. In the text there is "absolutely nothing" except symbolism that someone interprets in their own way. Symbolism here means only one thing: this is a man who should be asked about the space. To deduce from this that Jesus announced the age of Aquarius after two thousand years of the age of Pisces, he says, is completely unfounded. Nevertheless, he admits that to someone who has not seriously gone through Sacred Scripture and reads only that sentence, such an interpretation can seem convincing.

Mark, the guest emphasizes, has an entirely different direction and does not expect any future new age. **The new age comes with Christ and His resurrection**, and after that follows what Jesus announces at the institution of the Eucharist: that He will drink new wine in the Kingdom of Heaven. That is the new age for Mark, not the age of Aquarius.

sections.subtitle: Zašto novom dobu treba stari tekst?
sections.screenshot_description: Gost postavlja pitanje zašto zagovornici doba vodenjaka traže potvrdu u Novom zavjetu
sections.content:
Stojić predviđa prigovor: „Kako vi to znate?“ Odgovor vidi u proučavanju Biblije u cjelini. Tko poznaje širu sliku, kontekst i način pisanja novozavjetnih tekstova, može donijeti utemeljen zaključak o tumačenju, umjesto da rečenicu izvuče iz konteksta.

Fra Ante Vučković smatra da je mnogo zanimljivije drugo pitanje: zašto se zagovornik doba vodenjaka uopće poziva na **Novi zavjet**? Ako je netko uvjeren da dolazi novo doba, zašto simboliku traži u tekstu koji je, po njegovoj logici, tekst prošlosti, tekst koji „pripada ribi“ i koji mu ništa ne znači? Takva potreba da se nešto utemelji u kršćanskom tekstu ili da se u njemu nađe simbolika koje ondje nema, prema gostu, pokazuje da takvi tumači **sami sebi nisu do kraja uvjerljivi**. Nemaju dovoljno snažnih argumenata, pa se oslanjaju na nešto vrlo rubno, na simboliku koje u samom tekstu i njegovu kontekstu nema.
sections.subtitle_en: Why Does the New Age Need an Old Text?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest poses the question of why proponents of the Age of Aquarius seek confirmation in the New Testament
sections.content_en:
Stojić anticipates an objection: "How do you know that?" He sees the answer in studying the Bible as a whole. Whoever knows the broader picture, the context, and the manner of writing of the New Testament texts can make a well-founded conclusion about the interpretation, instead of taking a sentence out of context.

Fra Ante Vučković considers another question to be much more interesting: why does a proponent of the Age of Aquarius appeal to the **New Testament** at all? If someone is convinced that a new age is coming, why do they look for symbolism in a text that is, by their logic, a text of the past, a text that "belongs to the fish" and means nothing to them? Such a need to ground something in a Christian text or to find in it a symbolism that is not there, according to the guest, shows that such interpreters **are not completely convincing to themselves**. They do not have sufficiently strong arguments, so they rely on something very marginal, on symbolism that is not in the text itself and its context.

sections.subtitle: Glad za smislom, zamor kršćanstva i neočekivana buđenja u Francuskoj i na Kosovu
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković govori o novokrštenicima u Francuskoj i povratku vjeri na Kosovu
sections.content:
Na pitanje što ljude navodi na takva tumačenja, sugovornici zajedno dolaze do istog odgovora: mnogi su **gladni smisla**. Fra Ante Vučković podsjeća da su biblijski tekstovi otvoreni svakome i da ljudi očito imaju potrebu smjestiti sebe u određeno razdoblje.

Gost smatra da new age pokret igra na jednoj prilično realnoj činjenici, a to je **zamor koji se dogodio u kršćanstvu**: zamor i odmak od izvornog razumijevanja teksta nakon dvije tisuće godina. Istodobno primjećuje da današnje vrijeme možda pokazuje novo buđenje, i to kroz posve neočekivane pojave:

- **Francuska**, gdje je velik broj mladih novokrštenika,
- **Kosovo**, područje velikim dijelom islamske vjeroispovijesti, gdje se dio mlađih ljudi želi vratiti vjeri svojih predaka iz vremena prije osmanlijske vlasti. Fra Ante to povezuje s potragom za dobrim načinom života i za vlastitim identitetom, a neki tu pojavu nazivaju **povratkom korijenima**.

Te su pojave, kaže gost, osobito zanimljive u zapadnom svijetu nakon velikog zamora i otpada od vjere. Prije nekoliko desetljeća bile su česte pesimistične i naizgled uvjerljive prognoze da „vjera blijedi“ i da će nestati. Sada se pokazuje da ljudi zapravo nemaju jasnu sposobnost predviđanja kamo će svijet u cjelini ići.
sections.subtitle_en: Hunger for Meaning, Fatigue of Christianity, and Unexpected Awakenings in France and Kosovo
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković speaks about neophytes in France and the return to faith in Kosovo
sections.content_en:
When asked what leads people to such interpretations, the interlocutors jointly arrive at the same answer: many are **hungry for meaning**. Fra Ante Vučković recalls that biblical texts are open to everyone and that people obviously have a need to situate themselves in a specific era.

The guest believes that the New Age movement plays on a fairly real fact, which is the **fatigue that occurred in Christianity**: fatigue and departure from the original understanding of the text after two thousand years. At the same time, he notes that present times perhaps show a new awakening, through completely unexpected phenomena:

- **France**, where there is a large number of young neophytes,
- **Kosovo**, an area largely of Islamic faith, where a portion of younger people want to return to the faith of their ancestors from the time before Ottoman rule. Fra Ante connects this with the search for a good way of life and for one's own identity, and some call this phenomenon a **return to roots**.

These phenomena, says the guest, are especially interesting in the Western world after great fatigue and apostasy from the faith. A few decades ago, pessimistic and seemingly convincing forecasts were frequent that "faith is fading" and will disappear. Now it turns out that people actually do not have a clear ability to predict where the world as a whole will go.

sections.subtitle: Novi zavjet ne nudi kalendar budućnosti, nego poziv na budnost
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da Novi zavjet ne daje precizne podatke o budućnosti nego poziva na budnost
sections.content:
Stojić duhovito povezuje razgovor s tekstom: ljudi ne mogu predvidjeti budućnost, za razliku od Isusa koji predviđa čovjeka s krčagom vode. Fra Ante Vučković nadovezuje se tvrdnjom da su Isusova predviđanja za naš svijet izrečena s **malo riječi i malo slika**. U Novom zavjetu nema jasnih i preciznih podataka o tome koliko neko doba traje, kada završava ni po kojim se znakovima prepoznaje.

Novi zavjet umjesto toga stalno upozorava na **budnost**:

- budnost nad vlastitim životom i načinom na koji se živi,
- svijest da život stoji pred Bogom,
- svijest da je život kratak,
- potrebu da se život uredi tako da se ne izgubi, ne propadne i ne prođe uzalud.

To su, prema gostu, osnovne upute kada je riječ o razdobljima vremena. Stojić zaključuje da je to dovoljno, a sve ostalo svrstava u kategoriju „Babe Vange“ i olakog predviđanja. Uz to dodaje da sve okolnosti koje utječu na budućnost ionako nije moguće predvidjeti.
sections.subtitle_en: The New Testament Does Not Offer a Calendar of the Future, but a Call to Vigilance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that the New Testament does not give precise data about the future, but calls for vigilance
sections.content_en:
Stojić wittily connects the conversation with the text: people cannot predict the future, unlike Jesus who foresees the man with the water jar. Fra Ante Vučković follows up with the assertion that Jesus' predictions for our world are uttered with **few words and few images**. In the New Testament there is no clear and precise information about how long a certain era lasts, when it ends, or by what signs it is recognized.

The New Testament instead constantly warns of **vigilance**:

- vigilance over one's own life and the way one lives,
- awareness that life stands before God,
- awareness that life is short,
- the need to order life so that it is not lost, does not perish, and does not pass in vain.

These are, according to the guest, the basic instructions when it comes to periods of time. Stojić concludes that this is enough, and categorizes everything else under "Baba Vanga" and easy fortune-telling. In addition, he adds that all circumstances affecting the future cannot be predicted anyway.

sections.subtitle: Blagovalište na katu i sve što se podrazumijevalo, a nije zapisano
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković opisuje dvoranu na katu u današnjem Jeruzalemu
sections.content:
Vraćajući se tekstu, Stanko Stojić navodi Isusove riječi o čovjeku koji će učenicima pokazati „na katu veliko blagovalište“, prostor već spremljen. Pita treba li taj detalj tumačiti simbolički, primjerice kao znak uzvišenog položaja u odnosu na prizemlje, ili ga treba čitati doslovno.

Fra Ante Vučković odgovara konkretno. U **Jeruzalemu** i danas postoji dvorana na katu, više puta rušena i ponovno građena, koja je relativno prostrana. U nju lako stane priprema za skupinu nešto veću od obitelji, a to je, prema gostu, važan podatak.

Zatim upozorava na mnoštvo **pretpostavki** koje stoje iza kratkog teksta. Podrazumijeva se da će netko odnijeti janje u unutarnje dvorište Hrama gdje će biti obredno žrtvovano, da mu se neće slomiti kosti i da će netko nabaviti i pripremiti gorko zelje. Te stvari nisu zapisane jer su bile dio svakodnevnog života. „Pripremiti pashalnu večeru“ značilo je pripremiti sve što ona traži:

- janje koje treba žrtvovati i ispeći,
- **gorko zelje**,
- **vino**,
- dvoranu uređenu za sjedenje za stolom.

Marko je smatrao da te pojedinosti nisu potrebne. Glavno mu je bilo da čitatelj zna kako je Isus imao posljednju večeru sa svojim učenicima, nakon koje odlazi u **Getsemanski vrt**, gdje će biti uhvaćen i gdje počinje ono što je najavljivao.
sections.subtitle_en: The Upper Room and Everything That Was Taken for Granted, but Not Written Down
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković describes the room upstairs in present-day Jerusalem
sections.content_en:
Returning to the text, Stanko Stojić cites Jesus' words about the man who will show the disciples "a large upper room," a space already prepared. He asks whether that detail should be interpreted symbolically, for example as a sign of an elevated position in relation to the ground floor, or whether it should be read literally.

Fra Ante Vučković answers concretely. In **Jerusalem** even today there is a room upstairs, demolished and rebuilt several times, which is relatively spacious. It easily accommodates preparations for a group somewhat larger than a family, and that is, according to the guest, important information.

Then he draws attention to the multitude of **assumptions** that stand behind the short text. It is taken for granted that someone will carry the lamb into the inner courtyard of the Temple where it will be ritually sacrificed, that none of its bones will be broken, and that someone will procure and prepare bitter herbs. These things are not written down because they were part of everyday life. "To prepare the Passover meal" meant preparing everything it requires:

- a lamb to be sacrificed and roasted,
- **bitter herbs**,
- **wine**,
- a hall arranged for sitting at table.

Mark considered that these details were not necessary. His main point was for the reader to know that Jesus had the Last Supper with His disciples, after which He goes to the **Garden of Gethsemane**, where He will be seized and where what He had announced begins.

sections.subtitle: „Da nisam ja?“: pitanje koje Marko upućuje svakom čitatelju
sections.screenshot_description: Gost tumači pitanje učenika „Da nisam ja?“ kao poziv na osobno ispitivanje savjesti
sections.content:
Drugi dio odlomka, prema fra Anti Vučkoviću, vrti se oko još jednog važnog detalja: **izdaje Učitelja**. To je snažan i dramatičan trenutak. Isus unaprijed zna da će Ga izdati jedan od onih koji s Njim blaguju, jedan koji zbog toga nije isključen i kojemu je mjesto za stolom otvoreno kao i svima ostalima.

U tom kontekstu gost upozorava na suptilnu nijansu koju donosi Marko. U ovom tekstu **uopće ne navodi tko je izdajnik**, ne imenuje Judu, a učenici ne pitaju „tko je to, Gospodine?“. Njihovo pitanje glasi: **„Da nisam ja?“** Svi ga redom postavljaju.

Kao da je Marko htio, tumači fra Ante, da se na kraju i sam čitatelj zapita: „Da nisam ja?“ Najvažnije nije znati tko je izdajnik, nego kako pojedinac stoji u odnosu prema Učitelju i ne izdaje li Ga možda on sam. Tekst je prema gostu napisan **za život onih koji čitaju** i za njihov odnos s Učiteljem, jer On nije prestao biti Učitelj. Drama jednog učenika mogućnost je u koju bi mogao upasti svaki učenik. Zato je važno da svatko postavi to pitanje, ili njegovu širu inačicu: „Da nije nešto u mom životu, u mojim riječima, u mojim postupcima nalik izdaji koju sad promatramo?“

Tako se, zaključuje gost, vidi kako je Marko oblikovao kratak opis pashalne večere. Manje važne stvari ostaju u pozadini i podrazumijevaju se, a u prvom su planu dramatski ključni elementi: večera, zajedništvo s učenicima, izdaja jednoga od njih i Isusovo uhićenje.
sections.subtitle_en: "Is It I?": The Question Mark Addresses to Every Reader
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest interprets the disciples' question "Is it I?" as a call to personal examination of conscience
sections.content_en:
The second part of the passage, according to fra Ante Vučković, revolves around another important detail: **the betrayal of the Teacher**. It is a powerful and dramatic moment. Jesus knows in advance that one of those dining with Him will betray Him, one who is not excluded because of that and to whom the place at the table is open just as to everyone else.

In that context, the guest draws attention to the subtle nuance brought by Mark. In this text, **he does not state at all who the traitor is**, does not name Judas, and the disciples do not ask "who is it, Lord?". Their question is: **"Is it I?"** They all ask it one by one.

It is as if Mark wanted, fra Ante interprets, for the reader himself in the end to ask: "Is it I?" The most important thing is not knowing who the traitor is, but where the individual stands in relation to the Teacher and whether he himself might not be betraying Him. The text, according to the guest, is written **for the life of those who read** and for their relationship with the Teacher, because He has not ceased to be the Teacher. The drama of one disciple is a possibility into which any disciple could fall. That is why it is important that everyone asks that question, or its broader version: "Might there be something in my life, in my words, in my actions resembling the betrayal we are now observing?"

Thus, the guest concludes, one sees how Mark shaped the short description of the Passover meal. Less important things remain in the background and are taken for granted, while in the foreground are the dramatically crucial elements: the supper, fellowship with the disciples, the betrayal by one of them, and Jesus' arrest.

sections.subtitle: Janje, krv i sakriveno klanje: koliko smo daleko od stvarnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Stanko Stojić govori o tome koliko je današnjem čovjeku teško zamisliti klanje janjeta
sections.content:
Na pitanje spominje li tekst još nešto na stolu osim kruha i vina, fra Ante Vučković odgovara da ne spominje, ali da je toga zasigurno bilo. Teško je zamisliti pashalnu večeru bez gorkog zelja. Da ga nije bilo, Marko bi vjerojatno naveo razlog. Pretpostavka je da je večera bila pripremljena onako kako se pashalna večera inače priprema.

Stanko Stojić primjećuje da je današnjem čovjeku teško zamisliti da netko uzme janje koje se otima i zakolje ga dok krv teče okolo. Takav bi opis danas djelovao brutalno i naturalistički. Fra Ante podsjeća da se janjci i danas kolju. Razlika je u tome što se to naučilo **skrivati**: radi to netko koga ne vidimo i na način koji nam nije prisutan. To je, međutim, jedini način na koji meso dolazi na stol. Svaka životinja na tanjuru prošla je kroz završetak života, klanje ili neki drugi način usmrćivanja, primjerice pištoljem, što je za samu poantu nevažno. Gost usput primjećuje da je i riječ **klaonica**, nekoć uobičajena, danas gotovo izblijedila. Bitno je da je životinja završila život kako bi ljudi mogli jesti.
sections.subtitle_en: The Lamb, Blood, and Hidden Slaughter: How Far We Are from Reality
sections.screenshot_description_en: Stanko Stojić speaks about how difficult it is for modern man to imagine the slaughter of a lamb
sections.content_en:
When asked whether the text mentions anything else on the table besides bread and wine, fra Ante Vučković answers that it does not mention it, but that it was certainly there. It is difficult to imagine a Passover meal without bitter herbs. Had there been none, Mark would probably have stated the reason. The assumption is that the meal was prepared the way a Passover meal is otherwise prepared.

Stanko Stojić notes that it is difficult for modern man to imagine someone taking a lamb that struggles and slaughtering it while blood flows around. Such a description today would seem brutal and naturalistic. Fra Ante recalls that lambs are slaughtered today as well. The difference is that one has learned to **hide** it: it is done by someone we do not see and in a manner that is not present to us. That is, however, the only way meat comes to the table. Every animal on the plate has gone through the end of life, slaughter or some other way of killing, for example with a stun gun, which is irrelevant to the point itself. The guest incidentally notes that even the word **slaughterhouse**, once common, has today almost faded. What matters is that the animal ended its life so that people could eat.

sections.subtitle: Rajčica koja „raste u trgovini“: gubitak kontakta sa živim svijetom
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković govori o ljudima koji nikad nisu vidjeli kako raste povrće
sections.content:
Stojić zaključuje da je čovjek danas cijeli taj proces gurnuo u apstrakciju i o njemu uopće ne razmišlja, jer mu je i samo zamišljanje prebrutalno. Fra Ante Vučković proširuje misao: to se nije dogodilo samo sa životinjama, nego i s **povrćem**. Dobar dio ljudi nikad nije vidio kako raste rajčica ili kupus, ni gdje raste jabuka. „U trgovini“, dobacuje voditelj, a gost prihvaća šalu: „Raste u trgovini.“

To, prema fra Anti, udaljava čovjeka od stvarnog života, a konkretan kontakt sa životom smatra vrlo važnim. Koliko taj kontakt nedostaje vidi se po tome koliko ljudi osjeća potrebu za **kućnim ljubimcem**, za životinjom u kući. Ljubimci su neka vrsta drugačijeg kontakta sa živim svijetom, ali s drugim naglaskom: to više nisu životinje koje se jedu.

Do nedavno su ljudi imali svakodnevan i stvaran odnos sa životinjama koje će sutradan jesti. Gost nabraja:

- ovce koje su se čuvale,
- kokoši po dvorištu,
- kravu koja je otelila tele koje je potom zaklano,
- zečeve i druge domaće životinje.

Danas su mnoga **sela opustjela**. Sve manje ljudi ima takav kontakt, a životinje sve češće dolaze iz masovnog uzgoja umjesto s malih obiteljskih farmi. Ponešto je, napominje gost, ostalo sa svinjama u **Slavoniji**. Ipak, velik dio ljudi to ne vidi i ne susreće, pa vjerojatno ni ne razmišlja odakle dolazi pršut ili pileća prsa na stolu. Stojić to naziva gubitkom kontakta s bitnim dijelom cijelog života i sustava te, aludirajući na naslov emisije „Jedno ti nedostaje“, zaključuje da nam nedostaje upravo taj kontakt sa životom.
sections.subtitle_en: A Tomato That "Grows in the Store": Loss of Contact with the Living World
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković speaks about people who have never seen how vegetables grow
sections.content_en:
Stojić concludes that man today has pushed that whole process into abstraction and does not think about it at all, because even the mere imagining of it is too brutal for him. Fra Ante Vučković broadens the thought: this has not happened only with animals, but also with **vegetables**. A good portion of people have never seen how a tomato or cabbage grows, nor where an apple grows. "In the store," the host interjects, and the guest takes up the joke: "It grows in the store."

That, according to fra Ante, distances man from real life, and he considers concrete contact with life to be very important. How much that contact is missing can be seen from how many people feel the need for a **pet**, for an animal in the house. Pets are a kind of different contact with the living world, but with a different emphasis: these are no longer animals that are eaten.

Until recently, people had a daily and real relationship with animals they would eat the next day. The guest lists:

- sheep that were tended,
- chickens around the yard,
- a cow that calved a calf that was then slaughtered,
- rabbits and other domestic animals.

Today many **villages are deserted**. Fewer and fewer people have such contact, and animals increasingly come from mass farming instead of small family farms. Something, the guest notes, has remained with pigs in **Slavonija**. Still, a large portion of people do not see this and do not encounter it, so they probably do not even think about where the prosciutto or chicken breast on the table comes from. Stojić calls this a loss of contact with an essential part of all life and the system, and, alluding to the title of the show "One Thing You Lack," concludes that what we lack is precisely that contact with life.

sections.subtitle: Krv kao život: starozavjetna simbolika koja tek slijedi
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava starozavjetno značenje krvi kao života
sections.content: Fra Ante Vučković ističe da je u pashalnom kontekstu kontakt s **krvlju** još uvijek vrlo prisutan. Najavljuje da će se u sljedećem odlomku Markova evanđelja pojaviti snažna simbolika krvi. U **Starom zavjetu** krv znači život, jer je život vezan uz krv koja kola kroz svaki dio tijela. Tom se napomenom otvara put prema temi koju serijal tek treba obraditi, ustanovi Euharistije.
sections.subtitle_en: Blood as Life: Old Testament Symbolism Yet to Come
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the Old Testament meaning of blood as life
sections.content_en: Fra Ante Vučković emphasizes that in the Passover context, contact with **blood** is still very present. He announces that in the next passage of the Gospel of Mark, powerful symbolism of blood will appear. In the **Old Testament**, blood means life, because life is bound to the blood that circulates through every part of the body. That remark opens the way to the topic that the series has yet to cover, the institution of the Eucharist.

sections.subtitle: Psalam 41 i Tolkienov suživot sa Svetim pismom
sections.screenshot_description: Stanko Stojić govori o Tolkienovoj biografiji i svakodnevnom suživotu sa Svetim pismom
sections.content:
Stanko Stojić upozorava na još jedan detalj. Isusove riječi „Kažem vam, jedan će me od vas izdati koji sa mnom blaguje“ u tekstu su istaknute i povezane s **Psalmom 41**. Stojić se prisjeća nedavno pročitane **Tolkienove biografije** u kojoj se opisuje piščev svakodnevni suživot sa Svetim pismom i važnost hranjenja Svetim pismom.

U Isusovu govoru, primjećuje voditelj, stalno izbija neki starozavjetni tekst, primjerice psalam. Moglo bi se reći da ga je pisac umetnuo kako bi potvrdio Stari zavjet, no Stojiću je važnije nešto drugo: Isus je **živio sa svetim tekstom**. To bi moglo biti uputa i današnjim vjernicima, da im u svakodnevni govor ne uđu samo citati kao citati, nego kao misli i duhovni sadržaj, pa da i kad govore, na neki način govore citirajući.
sections.subtitle_en: Psalm 41 and Tolkien's Living with Sacred Scripture
sections.screenshot_description_en: Stanko Stojić speaks about Tolkien's biography and daily living with Sacred Scripture
sections.content_en:
Stanko Stojić draws attention to yet another detail. Jesus' words "Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me, one who is eating with me" are emphasized in the text and connected with **Psalm 41**. Stojić recalls a recently read **biography of Tolkien** in which the author's daily living with Sacred Scripture and the importance of feeding on Sacred Scripture are described.

In Jesus' speech, the host notes, some Old Testament text constantly surfaces, for example a psalm. One could say that the writer inserted it to confirm the Old Testament, but something else is more important to Stojić: Jesus **lived with the sacred text**. That could also be an instruction for today's believers, that not only quotes as quotes enter their daily speech, but as thoughts and spiritual content, so that even when they speak, they speak in a certain way by quoting.

sections.subtitle: Kako je Biblija oblikovala hrvatski jezik
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković govori o biblijskim metaforama u hrvatskom jeziku
sections.content: Fra Ante Vučković potvrđuje da su u židovskom svijetu raniji sveti tekstovi ušli u svakodnevni govor, u maštu, u metafore i u način na koji su ljudi razumijevali sami sebe. Isto vrijedi i za **hrvatski jezik**, koji je, kaže, prožet mnoštvom slika i metafora iz biblijskog svijeta. Prevođenjem **Biblije** na hrvatski jezik širio se i produbljivao sam jezik. Gost to smatra važnim za razumijevanje razvoja hrvatskog jezika.
sections.subtitle_en: How the Bible Shaped the Croatian Language
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković speaks about biblical metaphors in the Croatian language
sections.content_en: Fra Ante Vučković confirms that in the Jewish world, earlier sacred texts entered daily speech, imagination, metaphors, and the way people understood themselves. The same applies to the **Croatian language**, which, he says, is permeated with a multitude of images and metaphors from the biblical world. By translating the **Bible** into the Croatian language, the language itself expanded and deepened. The guest considers this important for understanding the development of the Croatian language.

sections.subtitle: Podignuta peta: izdaja koja dolazi od zajedničkog stola
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava starozavjetnu sliku podizanja pete na pobijeđenog
sections.content:
Na primjeru Psalma 41 fra Ante Vučković pokazuje snagu biblijske slike. U psalmu stoji: „Prijatelj moj koji sa mnom blagovaše, petu na me podiže.“ Gost tu sliku naziva **ekstremno jakom**. Podići petu na nečiju glavu značilo je učiniti ga robom, potpuno sebi podložnim.

Tako su postupali kraljevi. Nakon pobjede nad drugim kraljevstvom pred njih bi doveli poražene plemiće i kraljeve, koji bi morali kleknuti, a pobjednik bi im podigao nogu na glavu. Poruka je bila: „Ti si meni posve podložan.“ Izdaja u tom svjetlu znači: „Ja te mogu uništiti, stavio sam te ispod svoje pete.“

Taj je trenutak, prema gostu, prisutan u pozadini Markova teksta jer **izdaja dolazi iz blizine**. Onaj koji s Isusom blaguje ponaša se kao da je iznad Njega, a dijeli s Njim hranu. To je najveća moguća izdaja, jer je dijeljenje istog stola i iste hrane osnovni izraz prijateljstva, blizine, ljubavi, povezanosti i međusobne zaštite. Ovdje se pokazuje nešto posve suprotno, i zato taj trenutak, ističe fra Ante, drastično udara u oči.
sections.subtitle_en: The Raised Heel: Betrayal Coming from the Shared Table
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the Old Testament image of raising one's heel against the defeated
sections.content_en:
Using the example of Psalm 41, fra Ante Vučković demonstrates the power of the biblical image. In the psalm it is written: "Even my friend who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me." The guest calls this image **extremely strong**. To lift a heel onto someone's head meant making him a slave, completely subject to oneself.

That is how kings acted. After a victory over another kingdom, defeated nobles and kings would be brought before them, who would have to kneel, and the victor would lift his foot onto their head. The message was: "You are completely subject to me." Betrayal in that light means: "I can destroy you, I have put you under my heel."

That moment, according to the guest, is present in the background of Mark's text because **betrayal comes from closeness**. The one who dines with Jesus acts as though he is above Him, yet he shares food with Him. That is the greatest possible betrayal, because sharing the same table and the same food is the fundamental expression of friendship, closeness, love, connection, and mutual protection. Here something completely opposite is shown, and that is why this moment, fra Ante emphasizes, drastically strikes the eyes.

sections.subtitle: Evanđelje kao temelj mišljenja i najdublje rane od bliskih ljudi
sections.screenshot_description: Stanko Stojić uspoređuje evanđelje s Francuskom revolucijom i Komunističkim manifestom kao duhovnim izvorima
sections.content:
Stanko Stojić smatra važnim osvijestiti nešto što se često zaboravlja: u temelju razmišljanja, rječnika i svakodnevice vjernika stoji **evanđeoski tekst**. Sasvim drukčije živi onaj kojemu je utemeljiteljski događaj ili duhovni izvor, primjerice, **Francuska revolucija**, **Komunistički manifest** ili neka politička ideja 20. stoljeća. Drugi je tada temelj i drugi duh iz kojega čovjek progovara. Kad je izvor evanđelje, kaže voditelj, otvara se i duh.

Fra Ante Vučković vraća se slici izdaje za stolom i naziva je **najdubljom ranom** koju ljudi mogu nanijeti jedni drugima: ranu ti nanosi netko s kim dijeliš stol. U današnjem svijetu, dodaje, možda je još češća rana koju nanosi netko s kim dijeliš postelju. To su najdublje boli, one koje proizlaze iz trenutka blizine.
sections.subtitle_en: The Gospel as the Foundation of Thinking and the Deepest Wounds from Close People
sections.screenshot_description_en: Stanko Stojić compares the Gospel with the French Revolution and the Communist Manifesto as spiritual sources
sections.content_en:
Stanko Stojić considers it important to become aware of something that is often forgotten: at the foundation of the thinking, vocabulary, and daily life of believers stands the **Gospel text**. A person whose foundational event or spiritual source is, for example, the **French Revolution**, the **Communist Manifesto**, or some political idea of the 20th century lives completely differently. The foundation is then different, and the spirit out of which a person speaks is different. When the source is the Gospel, says the host, the spirit also opens.

Fra Ante Vučković returns to the image of betrayal at the table and calls it **the deepest wound** that people can inflict on one another: a wound is inflicted on you by someone with whom you share a table. In today's world, he adds, perhaps even more frequent is a wound inflicted by someone with whom you share a bed. Those are the deepest pains, those that arise from a moment of closeness.

sections.subtitle: Prikriveni izdajnik i Isus koji štiti i onoga koji Ga izdaje
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković objašnjava kako se izdajnik skriva iza pitanja koje postavljaju svi učenici
sections.content:
Fra Ante Vučković ponovno ističe Učiteljevu svijest o tome što će Mu se dogoditi, uz šutnju o tome tko će to učiniti. Može se pretpostaviti da onaj koji je već zakoračio u izdaju zna o kome je riječ, ali ostaje **prikriven i šuti**. U Matejevu evanđelju ponavlja isto pitanje koje postavljaju svi: „Da nisam ja, Učitelju?“ Skriva se iza istog jezika kojim govore ostali učenici.

Marko ga, prema gostu, ostavlja zaštićenim, a pitanje „Da nisam ja?“ usmjerava prema svakom pojedincu. Ono se tiče svakoga.

Stanko Stojić u tome vidi trajnu Isusovu nakanu da **zaštiti čak i onoga koji Ga izdaje**. Primjećuje i književnu snagu prizora: izdaja smještena usred intimne večere jače odjekuje, a spoj intime i izdaje vrlo je učinkovit.
sections.subtitle_en: The Concealed Traitor and Jesus Who Protects Even the One Who Betrays Him
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković explains how the traitor hides behind the question asked by all the disciples
sections.content_en:
Fra Ante Vučković once again emphasizes the Teacher's awareness of what will happen to Him, along with silence about who will do it. It can be assumed that the one who has already stepped into betrayal knows who it is about, but remains **concealed and silent**. In the Gospel of Matthew, he repeats the same question that everyone asks: "Is it I, Teacher?" He hides behind the same language spoken by the other disciples.

Mark, according to the guest, leaves him protected, and directs the question "Is it I?" toward each individual. It concerns everyone.

Stanko Stojić sees in this Jesus' enduring intention to **protect even the one who betrays Him**. He also notes the literary power of the scene: betrayal placed in the midst of an intimate supper resonates more strongly, and the combination of intimacy and betrayal is very effective.

sections.subtitle: „Bolje bi mu bilo da se ni rodio nije“: Božji plan i ljudska sloboda
sections.screenshot_description: Gost tumači paradoks Božjeg upravljanja poviješću i Judine slobode
sections.content:
Stojić upozorava na još jedan težak detalj, Isusove riječi: „Tome bi čovjeku bolje bilo da se ni rodio nije.“ Pita mogu li te riječi značiti osudu, iako Crkva Judu nikada nije službeno smjestila u pakao.

Fra Ante Vučković objašnjava da je riječ o vrlo važnoj misli izrečenoj na **paradoksalan način**, koja drži zajedno dvije istine:

- **povijest ide prema Božjem planu**, prema kojemu će Isus dati svoj život na križu,
- to **ne umanjuje odgovornost ni slobodu ljudi**, u ovom slučaju Judinu.

Drugim riječima, Juda nije bio predodređen da bude izdajnik, ali ni on nije bio odlučujući za ono što će se dogoditi s Isusom. Treba istodobno držati da Bog upravlja poviješću, da Isus sam svjesno odlučuje poći tim putem i da je Juda ipak mogao postupiti drukčije: bio je slobodan i sam je donio svoju odluku. U tom svjetlu, kaže gost, treba razumjeti rečenicu o čovjeku koji Ga predaje.
sections.subtitle_en: "It Would Be Better for Him If He Had Not Been Born": God's Plan and Human Freedom
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest interprets the paradox of God's governance of history and Judas' freedom
sections.content_en:
Stojić draws attention to yet another difficult detail, Jesus' words: "It would have been better for that man if he had not been born." He asks whether those words can mean condemnation, even though the Church has never officially placed Judas in hell.

Fra Ante Vučković explains that this is a very important thought expressed in a **paradoxical way**, which holds together two truths:

- **history moves according to God's plan**, according to which Jesus will lay down His life on the cross,
- this **does not diminish the responsibility or freedom of people**, in this case Judas'.

In other words, Judas was not predestined to be a traitor, but neither was he decisive for what would happen with Jesus. One must hold simultaneously that God governs history, that Jesus Himself consciously decides to go along that path, and that Judas could nevertheless have acted differently: he was free and made his decision himself. In that light, the guest says, the sentence about the man who betrays Him should be understood.

sections.subtitle: Judina sudbina: kajanje, samoosuda i pogled koji nije susreo
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Ante Vučković uspoređuje Judino kajanje i samoosudu s Petrovim susretom s Učiteljevim pogledom
sections.content:
Fra Ante Vučković naglašava da rečenica „bolje bi mu bilo da se ni rodio nije“ **ni u kojem slučaju ne proglašava** Judu sinom propasti koji je već propao. Evanđelja ne daju uvid u to što se s Judom na kraju dogodilo. Zna se da je njegov čin bio izdaja, ali njegova konačna sudbina ostaje skrivena Bogu, kao i sudbina svakog čovjeka. U katoličkom se svijetu uvijek može misliti da se u posljednjoj sekundi prije smrti možda promijenio stav.

Gost podsjeća da **Matej** piše kako se Juda pokajao, vratio novac i priznao pogrešku. Ono što mu je nedostajalo i što je bilo odlučujuće za njegovu sudbinu jest to što je **ostao sam sa svojom samoosudom**. Fra Ante to stanje naziva možda najtežim u koje čovjek može upasti. Juda se nije susreo s Učiteljevim pogledom, za razliku od **Petra**, koji će se kasnije s tim pogledom susresti.

Ipak se ne može tvrditi da se u posljednjem trenutku nije nešto dogodilo u Judinoj svijesti ili u njegovu odnosu s Učiteljem što je odredilo kamo će otići. Duga povijest kršćanstva, priznaje gost, vidjela je Judu kao sina izdaje, kao nekoga tko je propao i izgubio vlastiti život iz velike blizine s Učiteljem. No njegovu konačnu sudbinu valja ostaviti u Božjim rukama.
sections.subtitle_en: Judas' Fate: Repentance, Self-Condemnation, and the Gaze He Did Not Meet
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Ante Vučković compares Judas' repentance and self-condemnation with Peter's encounter with the Teacher's gaze
sections.content_en:
Fra Ante Vučković emphasizes that the sentence "it would be better for him if he had not been born" **by no means proclaims** Judas as a son of perdition who is already lost. The Gospels do not provide insight into what happened to Judas in the end. It is known that his act was betrayal, but his final fate remains hidden to God, as is the fate of every human being. In the Catholic world, one can always think that in the last second before death, perhaps the attitude changed.

The guest recalls that **Matthew** writes how Judas repented, returned the money, and admitted his mistake. What he lacked and what was decisive for his fate is that he **remained alone with his self-condemnation**. Fra Ante calls this condition perhaps the most difficult into which a person can fall. Judas did not meet the Teacher's gaze, unlike **Peter**, who will later meet that gaze.

Yet one cannot claim that in the final moment something did not happen in Judas' consciousness or in his relationship with the Teacher that determined where he would go. The long history of Christianity, the guest admits, saw Judas as a son of betrayal, as someone who was lost and threw away his own life out of great closeness with the Teacher. But his ultimate fate should be left in God's hands.

sections.subtitle: Sad je život: ne čekati bolje vrijeme za one koje volimo
sections.screenshot_description: Gost poziva gledatelje da odmah pronađu vremena za bliske odnose
sections.content:
Za kraj emisije Stanko Stojić izdvaja jednu misao. Neposredno prije najtežih životnih trenutaka, i Isusovih i osobnih, možda je dobro provesti vrijeme s ljudima koje voliš, za večerom, za zajedničkim stolom.

Fra Ante Vučković priznaje da je ovdje prikazan dobar način odlaska s ovoga svijeta, ali podsjeća da malo tko zna kada će otići iz ovoga života. Zato je važnije za bliske odnose naći **vremena, pozornosti i prostora dok je to još moguće**. Treba izbjeći klopku razmišljanja da će kasnije doći bolje vrijeme u kojem će se moći bolje i pametnije činiti dobro. Dobro treba činiti sada, dok je za to prostor otvoren.

Stojić emisiju zaključuje porukom gledateljima: „Sad je život. Sad. Ne sutra. Sad počinje život.“ Zahvaljuje gostu i najavljuje susret u sljedećoj epizodi.
sections.subtitle_en: Now Is Life: Not Waiting for a Better Time for Those We Love
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest calls upon viewers to find time immediately for close relationships
sections.content_en:
For the end of the show, Stanko Stojić highlights one thought. Immediately before the most difficult moments of life, both Jesus' and personal ones, perhaps it is good to spend time with the people you love, at supper, at a shared table.

Fra Ante Vučković admits that a good way of departing from this world is shown here, but recalls that hardly anyone knows when they will depart from this life. That is why it is more important to find **time, attention, and space for close relationships while it is still possible**. One should avoid the trap of thinking that a better time will come later in which one will be able to do good better and more wisely. Good should be done now, while the space for it is open.

Stojić concludes the broadcast with a message to viewers: "Now is life. Now. Not tomorrow. Now life begins." He thanks the guest and announces the meeting in the next episode.
